title: 'We could have been dead,' says tenant who escaped Cape Breton building collapse
summary: Viola Baker says she was in bed Wednesday morning when she heard a big bang, and all of a sudden the walls started caving in. She rushed to help rescue her daughter and 15-year-old grandson.

image.caption: Viola Baker was a tenant in the building that collapsed and burned on Wednesday. (Kyle Moore/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia
Viola Baker says she was in bed Wednesday morning when she heard a big bang, and all of a sudden the walls started caving in. She rushed to help rescue her daughter and 15-year-old grandson.
Viola Baker says she's amazed everyone survived the incident
A woman who survived an explosion and the collapse of her apartment building in Glace Bay, N.S., on Wednesday says she's amazed everyone survived.
An explosion rocked the building at 130 Commercial St. around 6 a.m., causing the collapse and fire.
The structure, which housed a pizza shop on the ground floor and apartments above, was destroyed.
Officials say all 24 people who lived in the building were accounted for, including 17 who had minor injuries.
Viola Baker was in bed around early Wednesday morning when she heard a big bang.
"That’s when everything started shaking and everything was all coming down," she said. "I didn't know what the hell was going on."
Baker said she could hear her daughter and 15-year-old grandson screaming for help, so she kicked their door open.
"When I got there, I opened up my eyes and said, 'Oh my god.' The whole front of the building was right in the room."
She said the fridge fell on top of her daughter and part of the roof and some pipes fell on her grandson's head.
The building at 130 Commercial St. in Glace Bay, N.S., was destroyed after an explosion and fire on Wednesday. (Ernie Bagnell)
Baker said a taxi driver helped them get out from the rubble.
She said she's grateful for the first responders and everyone who has helped her family and the other tenants.
"So help me God, I don’t know how anybody walked. I was so happy that we all did and that we all got out," she said.
"It could have been worse. We could have been dead."
Baker said in the aftermath of the incident on Wednesday she wasn't in pain, but on Thursday she has pain in her back and bruises have started to appear.
She said she has lost everything. Her grandson has been especially concerned about the loss of his Xbox, Nintendo Switch and his collection of 72 wrestler figurines.
"There's a lot of stuff that can be replaced, but their lives couldn't," Baker said of the tenants.
John Marr lived on the main floor of the building. He said he was asleep at the time of the explosion.

"I figured it was a building across the road from me and when I got up, I seen no window, a big hole in the wall. When I looked to my right, I seen the red flames and I said that's fire — I'm getting out," Marr told CBC News.
Marr said he had to crawl to get out of the building without his shoes. He said his right hand was cut and his body is sore. He said he lost everything, including his wallet and a safe with his will.
Marr said he's glad everybody made it out, but that he's in shock. He said he's worried about finding a new place to live because winter is coming.
